headline: 3-4 on 7 value plays, -$8.32
paragraphs: Week 9 put 9 graded games in front of the model. It found a playable edge in 4 of them and left the other 5 alone. Those plays went 3-4, worth -$8.32 at $10 a play (-11.9% on the $70 at risk).

By market, spreads went 1-2, totals went 1-1 and moneylines went 1-1. The best of them was Over 47 in Tulane at Charlotte, a 4.9-point disagreement with the market that finished Tulane 38, Charlotte 31. The one that stung was Under 78 in Florida Atlantic at North Texas, a 12.4-point disagreement with the market that finished North Texas 48, Florida Atlantic 41.

The five plays that actually got published went 0-2 for -$20.00, behind the full board. Ranking by expected value is supposed to concentrate the good ones at the top, and whether it does is something only a season of these will answer.

Season to date the model has made 322 value plays and gone 137-177-8, -$424.82 on flat $10 bets (-13.2%). It expected to win 60% of those and won 44%. On line movement, 4 of the 13 published picks whose numbers moved closed worse than the site posted them, so the market came our way 31% of the time. Sample is getting real enough to argue with, though a model that beats closing lines is rarer than one that beats a few hundred results.
